subject: ela
intro: This quiz checks whether you can analyze how a part of an informational text fits into the whole and how it helps develop the ideas. Read each embedded passage closely, then choose the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

"To start a campfire safely, follow these steps. First, clear a circle of bare ground and ring it with stones. Next, place small twigs and dry leaves in the center. Then, lean larger sticks over the twigs like a tent. Finally, light the leaves and let the flame climb to the bigger sticks."

Which text structure does the author use to organize this paragraph?
A) Compare and contrast
B) Sequence (steps in order)
C) Cause and effect
D) Problem and solution

steps: The signal words First, Next, Then, and Finally show the author is listing steps in the order they must happen.
B is correct because the paragraph presents a process as an ordered series of steps, which is sequence structure.
A is wrong because the author never sets two things side by side to show likenesses and differences.
C is wrong because the paragraph does not explain why something happens as a result of something else; it lists steps to follow.
D is wrong because no problem is raised and then solved; the paragraph simply gives directions in order.

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

"Honeybees are vital to our food supply. They pollinate crops, support healthy ecosystems, and produce honey that people have valued for thousands of years. This article explains the many ways these small insects shape the world around us."

Where does this paragraph most likely fit in the structure of the whole article?
A) It is the introduction, because it names the topic and previews what the article will explain.
B) It is the conclusion, because it sums up the article and gives a final thought.
C) It is a body paragraph, because it gives one detailed example to support a point.
D) It is a transition, because it shifts the reader from one side of a comparison to another.
items.answer: A) It is the introduction, because it names the topic and previews what the article will explain.

steps: The paragraph names the topic (honeybees) and says This article explains, which previews what is coming.
A is correct because naming the topic and previewing the rest of the text is the job of an introduction.
B is wrong because the paragraph looks forward to what the article will explain rather than wrapping it up.
C is wrong because it states broad ideas about the topic instead of one detailed supporting example.
D is wrong because it does not move between two sides of a comparison; it opens the topic.
solution.answer: A) It is the introduction, because it names the topic and previews what the article will explain.

items.prompt:
Read the paragraph.

"Many city parks now plant native wildflowers instead of plain grass. For example, the new garden along River Street is filled with purple coneflowers and black-eyed Susans. These flowers feed local bees and need very little water to survive."

What job does the sentence beginning with "For example" do in this paragraph?
A) It states the main idea of the paragraph.
B) It gives a specific example that supports the main idea.
C) It introduces a brand new topic.
D) It draws a final conclusion for the whole article.
items.answer: B) It gives a specific example that supports the main idea.

steps: The words For example signal that the sentence is about to back up a larger point with a specific case.
B is correct because the River Street garden is a concrete instance of the claim that parks now plant native wildflowers.
A is wrong because the first sentence states the main idea; this sentence supports it.
C is wrong because the example stays on the same topic rather than introducing a new one.
D is wrong because the sentence supplies evidence in the middle, not a closing conclusion.
solution.answer: B) It gives a specific example that supports the main idea.

items.prompt:
Read the section.

"Sea otters may look like nothing more than playful swimmers, but they hold their entire coastal home together. Off the Pacific coast, otters feed on sea urchins. Without otters, urchin populations explode. The hungry urchins then chew through kelp forests until the underwater forests vanish. When the kelp disappears, the fish, crabs, and seabirds that depend on it lose their shelter and food. Because otters keep urchins in check, the whole web of life along the coast stays balanced."

How does the final sentence (beginning with "Because otters") contribute to the development of the ideas in this section?
A) It introduces a new and unrelated topic about seabirds.
B) It restates the chain of effects as a cause, tying the details back to the main idea that otters hold the habitat together.
C) It simply repeats the first sentence word for word.
D) It lists one more example of an animal that eats urchins.
items.answer: B) It restates the chain of effects as a cause, tying the details back to the main idea that otters hold the habitat together.

steps: The section builds a cause-and-effect chain: no otters lead to more urchins, which destroy kelp, which harms other animals.
B is correct because the final sentence sums up that chain with Because, linking the details back to the opening claim that otters hold their home together.
A is wrong because seabirds were already part of the section, and the sentence connects ideas rather than starting a new topic.
C is wrong because the sentence states a conclusion about cause and effect, not a word-for-word repeat of the opening.
D is wrong because it does not add another urchin-eating animal; it draws the whole section together.
solution.answer: B) It restates the chain of effects as a cause, tying the details back to the main idea that otters hold the habitat together.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"For years, students at Lincoln Middle School threw away mountains of paper, plastic, and food scraps every day. The overflowing trash bins were ugly, and the school paid rising fees to haul the waste away.

However, last fall a group of sixth graders proposed a school-wide recycling and composting program. They set up labeled bins, trained classmates to sort their waste, and partnered with a local farm to collect food scraps. Within months, the school's trash was cut nearly in half."

What is the purpose of the sentence that begins with "However" at the start of the second paragraph?
A) It states the main idea of the first paragraph.
B) It signals a shift from describing the problem to presenting a solution.
C) It gives one more detail about how much the school paid for trash hauling.
D) It concludes the passage by summing up everything that happened.
items.answer: B) It signals a shift from describing the problem to presenting a solution.

steps: The first paragraph describes a problem: too much waste, ugly bins, and rising fees.
The word However marks a turn, and the second paragraph describes the students' recycling and composting plan.
B is correct because the sentence moves the text from the problem to the solution, which is the structural job of this transition.
A is wrong because it does not restate the first paragraph; it points the reader toward something new.
C is wrong because it does not add a detail about hauling fees; it introduces the solution.
D is wrong because it appears in the middle and opens the solution rather than concluding the passage.
solution.answer: B) It signals a shift from describing the problem to presenting a solution.

items.prompt:
Read the section.

"Volcanoes can be deadly, but they are also builders. When a volcano erupts, molten rock called lava pours out and slowly hardens into new land. Over thousands of years, layer upon layer of cooled lava can stack up until a brand new island rises from the sea. The Hawaiian Islands, for instance, were formed this way. Today these islands are covered in rich soil, because volcanic rock breaks down into minerals that plants love."

What structural job does the sentence "The Hawaiian Islands, for instance, were formed this way" do in this section?
A) It is the main idea that the rest of the section supports.
B) It provides a real example that makes the general claim about volcanoes building land more convincing.
C) It signals a contrast that disagrees with the sentence before it.
D) It introduces a new topic about soil and farming.
items.answer: B) It provides a real example that makes the general claim about volcanoes building land more convincing.

steps: The section first makes a general claim: volcanoes build new land as lava hardens.
The phrase for instance shows the Hawaiian Islands are offered as a real case of that claim.
B is correct because a concrete example supports and strengthens the general idea about volcanoes building land.
A is wrong because the main idea is the earlier claim that volcanoes are builders; this sentence supports it.
C is wrong because the sentence agrees with and illustrates the point rather than contrasting with it.
D is wrong because soil is mentioned only afterward, and this sentence stays on the topic of building land.
solution.answer: B) It provides a real example that makes the general claim about volcanoes building land more convincing.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Every winter, the small town of Maple Ridge faced the same trouble. Heavy snow buried the roads, and the town owned only one aging plow. Drivers were often stranded for days, deliveries stopped, and the elderly could not reach the clinic. Year after year, residents complained, but nothing changed.

Last year, the town council finally acted. They voted to buy two new plows and to train a team of volunteer drivers. They also set up a phone alert system to warn residents before each storm. This winter, even after the largest snowfall in a decade, every road was cleared within hours, and not a single resident was left stranded."

Why did the author most likely describe the town's problem fully in the first paragraph before presenting the solution in the second?
A) Because describing the problem first gives the reader a reason to care, so the solution feels necessary rather than random.
B) Because the order of the paragraphs does not matter and could easily be reversed.
C) Because the first paragraph is meant to be the conclusion of the passage.
D) Because the author wanted to compare two different towns side by side.
items.answer: A) Because describing the problem first gives the reader a reason to care, so the solution feels necessary rather than random.

steps: The passage uses a problem-and-solution structure: paragraph one lays out the snow trouble, paragraph two gives the council's fix.
A is correct because stating the problem first makes the reader feel the stakes, so the new plows and alert system seem like a needed answer instead of an arbitrary choice.
B is wrong because the order does matter; the solution only feels meaningful once the reader understands the problem it solves.
C is wrong because the first paragraph opens the passage by raising the problem, not concluding it.
D is wrong because the passage focuses on one town across two times, not a comparison of two towns.
solution.answer: A) Because describing the problem first gives the reader a reason to care, so the solution feels necessary rather than random.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"There are good reasons to support a longer school year. Students forget a great deal of what they learn over a long summer break, and teachers spend weeks each fall reviewing old material. Countries with longer school years often score higher on international tests. A longer year would also give working families fewer weeks to arrange expensive summer childcare.

Still, a longer school year carries real costs. Buildings without air conditioning become unbearable in late summer heat. Family vacations and summer jobs would shrink. Teachers, already stretched thin, would face more weeks of work, and many schools cannot afford the higher pay and energy bills a longer year demands."

The author opens the second paragraph with the word "Still." How does this structural choice shape the development of the ideas in the passage?
A) It repeats the benefits listed in the first paragraph using different words.
B) It signals a shift to the opposing side, turning the passage into a balanced comparison of the benefits and the costs of a longer school year.
C) It proves that a longer school year is clearly the wrong choice.
D) It introduces an unrelated topic about air conditioning in homes.
items.answer: B) It signals a shift to the opposing side, turning the passage into a balanced comparison of the benefits and the costs of a longer school year.

steps: The first paragraph lists benefits of a longer school year, and the second lists costs, so the passage is built as a comparison of two sides.
The word Still marks the turn from the benefits to the drawbacks.
B is correct because Still signals the shift to the opposing side and shows the author is weighing both the benefits and the costs in a balanced way.
A is wrong because the second paragraph presents costs, not a reworded repeat of the benefits.
C is wrong because the passage presents both sides fairly rather than proving one side wrong.
D is wrong because air conditioning is mentioned as one cost within the school topic, not as an unrelated new subject.
solution.answer: B) It signals a shift to the opposing side, turning the passage into a balanced comparison of the benefits and the costs of a longer school year.
